notes: Service running on :8601 against the REAL throughline substrate, with REAL hosted judgments. /healthz reports judgment_source=hosted, judgment_model=nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b, substrate=real, mock=false. An earlier revision of this file said the judgment source was MOCK and blamed an age-recipient entitlement on the shared secret store; that blocker is withdrawn — the workstation now decrypts .secrets/nvidia-env.yaml with sops, the key exports, and judgments run. The quote validator is deterministic and model-free by design: digit-group spaces normalize outside quotation marks only, so text the source itself quoted is never rewritten to make a match succeed. An uncited judgment is regenerated once and then abstained on — the rejected finding is discarded, never republished at lower confidence. The same validator judges the hosted model that judges the mock; the real model is not given an easier bar.

Both halves are now false and were checked before this file was rewritten: in ~/source/git.infra/shared-secrets, sops -d --extract on the env.NVIDIA_API_KEY path of .secrets/nvidia-env.yaml exits 0 and yields the key, and the judgments above ran with it. known_limitations: SMC Title 23 grounding descoped (F5 bot wall, verified 2026-08-15). docket quotes the permit record itself, never the municipal code.
No embedding index is built; the corpus is small enough to serve directly, so llama-nemotron-embed-1b-v2 (dim 2048) is configured but unused.

The hosted model is not reliably parseable. In the 12-permit live run, 5 of 12 responses from nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b were not valid JSON and docket abstained on them rather than guessing at the content. That is the designed behaviour and it is also a real ceiling on yield: roughly half the corpus judges on any given pass.
The demo path replays from data/cache/. Seven hosted responses are committed so the demo runs offline; a permit outside that set needs a live key to judge.
